scope: Author-led comparison of the executable library model with the locally available primary full text. This is not an independent reproduction of the source analysis.

resultDefinitions.ARTICLE_ALIGNED: Published structure, fixed effects, covariates, variability and residual model are represented without an identified structural adaptation.
resultDefinitions.DOCUMENTED_ADAPTATION_CONFIRMED: The executable model differs from the publication, and the difference is explicitly documented in catalog metadata.
resultDefinitions.SOURCE_AMBIGUITY_DOCUMENTED: The publication contains an ambiguity that cannot be resolved without the source control stream or supplementary model files.

reviewed.note: The executable file represents the base model from Table 2, not the final covariate model. It remains simulation-only.
Two-compartment structure, creatinine-clearance effect, variability and proportional residual error align with the article. The zero additive variance only satisfies the two-term engine contract.
Fixed and random-effect values align with Table 2; the oral transit chain remains a reconstruction because executable transit equations are absent from the main article.
The source NPAG model is nonparametric; the log-normal OMEGA prior is an explicit mapbayr approximation.
The final unbound-concentration equations, including the published Q exponent 0.78, are retained. Published occasion variability is omitted.
Structure, dialysis branch, fixed effects and log-normal variance conversion align with the publication.
The two-compartment equations, dialysis, sex and infection effects and LC-MS/MS residual error align with the publication.
Published fixed effects and between-subject variability are retained; inter-occasion variability on CL and V1 is omitted.
The publication is ambiguous about lean versus total body weight for V; the engine's total-weight choice is documented.
The article does not provide the exact corrected lean-body-mass and Cockcroft-Gault variants; the implemented choices are documented.
Cockcroft-Gault substitution, albumin bounds and unreported Q/V2 allometric assumptions are documented engine adaptations.
Clinical formulas are reconstructed from available covariates; unreported covariance and V1 variability are not invented.
Clinical formulas are reconstructed from available covariates; unreported covariance and V1 variability are not invented.
One-compartment oral structure, renal and age covariates, variability and residual error align with the article.
The irreversible bone compartment is omitted for repeated-dose plasma simulation, and unpublished residual terms are marked pragmatic.
The publication reports an individual PK analysis; its use as a population prior is an explicit simulation-only adaptation.
Oral bioavailability and the female Cockcroft-Gault factor are engine assumptions; the published platelet PD component is out of scope.
The printed BMI effect on CL lacks an operator before 6.22; the retained historical interpretation is explicitly flagged.
One-compartment oral structure and reported fixed, random and residual parameters align with the article.
The final additive estimate 2.256 mg/L is implemented as an SD and squared for mrgsolve. The article also mentions log-transformed data despite its concentration-scale equation.
Structure and covariates align with the article. CL OMEGA is converted consistently from the published 39.8% CV using log(1 + CV^2).
The Revilla equations, measured 24-hour creatinine clearance and additive residual SD align with the article.
The continuous-infusion structure, measured 24-hour creatinine clearance and published parameter values align with the article.
